column2: Normal gems can be socketed into the gem slots of your secondary gear. the gear pieces offer different amounts of slots and color possibilities.
the maximum amount of socketed normal gems is 20. if you have upgraded your normal gems to a high level (6+) it is worth considering the amount of gem slots
when farming for secondary gear. It does not matter as much if you cant socket a rank 4 Saphire that gives you 36 armor penetration,
but missing out on a rank 7 saphire with 368 armor penetration might be noticeable in some content.
you can upgrade normal gems at the apprentice jeweler. from rank 1 to rank 5 you only need other copies to upgrade your gems. .
from rank 5 to rank 10 you need 1-X additional "echo crystals" that you can buy at the crystal vendor in westmarch next to the Jeweler. those crystals cost 500 platinum each
normal gems can be bound or unbound (you can see a tiny market symbol on the gem if it is unbound). the unbound gems can be sold at the market.

for tourmaline and ruby the stat gain for each upgrade is neglectible compared to other methods of improving your damage / life stats like the paragon trees.
(for example 5 paragon points invested = 100 damage which is more than a rank 5 tourmaline).
the other gems do gain you a significant amount of secondary attribute stats.
for blue and yellow gems, the jump in stats from Rank 5->6 and 6->7 are huge upgrades.
Upgrading normal gems until R7 is "ok" in terms of cost / value ratio. Afterwards it becomes expensive
If the average Platinum price for Saphires is around 200 and you buy 729 gems from the marketplace, that's 145800 platinum for a R7 gem, 437400 for a R8 gem, which is around 583€
A fully maxed out character with 6 x red, 6 yellow and 8 blue Gems has spent (at minimum) around 64.500€, more likely around 100.000€ because prices for normal gems were higher the first 2 years
Only upgrade Gems if you have an additional replacement Gem, otherwise you might end up with less secondary stats than before the upgrade
The sum of the ranks of your gems after the upgrade has to be equal or higher than the sum of ranks before.
e.g. 3 x Rank 8 Gems (3x8 = 24) need to be replaced with at least 9+8+7 = 24.
For example, if you want to upgrade one of your Rank 8 Saphires and you have 2 Rank 8 Saphires in Slots, you need 1 Rank 8 Saphire for the Upgrade, and afterwards
you need at least a Rank 7 Saphire for the empty Slot to get +8 Armor Penetration. So it only makes sense to upgrade the Rank 8 Saphire if you have another Rank 8
Saphire for the Slot to get a noticeable upgrade of +296 Armor Penetration
So the sum of the ranks of your gems after the upgrade has to be equal or higher than the sum of ranks before.
The Refinement Attribute of normal gems is a fixed percentage bonus that increases the base attribute of the set item equipment piece it is slotted into
It is calculated by the following formulas:
Bonus = 0.03 * sum of ranks of slotted gems * BASE_LIFE of Set Piece
Bonus = 0.03 * sum of ranks of slotted gems * BASE_DMG of Set Piece
Since Damage is only found on Hands it makes sense to slot your highest yellow gems here
Waist and Feet have the highest base life value so you should slot your highest red (waist) and blue (feet) gems here
Only the Hand gives a damage bonus, so finding a Set Piece with 3 yellow sockets is a priority when comparing gear pieces
more gem slots & higher ranked gems slotted in will increase your damage - so put your highest ranked yellow gems into your hand set piece
Normal gems can either be bought with platinum on the market or be optained via various activities / rewards in the game.
open world farming in a group of 4 can get you a maximum of 12 gems /day.
doing hidden lairs or castle ereban / abyssal verge each week (solo or in a party) get you max 126 (21x6 normal gems: 63 bound / 63 unbound).
other sources are the HILTS vendor or rewards for limited time events.
you can spend money to buy normal gems in the shop but since there are plenty of F2P sources it does not make sense.
Assuming you get 600 gems per month and they are evenly spread, you will have 100 gems per color per month.
